source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Draw NPH insulin first and regular insulin second, so the clear vial receives a small amount of cloudy suspension.","B":"Draw regular insulin first and NPH insulin second when the prescribed products are compatible for syringe mixing.","C":"Mix the vial contents together before drawing either insulin, so each vial contains the same final concentration.","D":"Draw the products in any order because contamination of the regular insulin vial cannot alter later dose characteristics."}}
source_row.rationale: When regular insulin and NPH are specifically ordered to be mixed, labeling instructs drawing regular insulin first and NPH second, then administering the mixture promptly.
source_row.source_detail: Administration instructions for mixing with regular insulin: draw regular insulin into the syringe first, followed by HUMULIN N; administer immediately after mixing. Current FDA/DailyMed Humulin N prescribing information rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A nurse is preparing a syringe containing regular insulin and NPH insulin. Which sequence is appropriate when the products are ordered to be mixed?
